s1.syndrome_frame: Postoperative skin lesion with erythema and nodules
salient_findings: Pruritic erythema lesion with multiple nodules over the operation site of the right breast
Well-demarcated, warm, erythematous plaque over the right side of the anterior chest wall
Multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels
key_facts: History of right breast cancer, stage IIIa (cT2N2M0)
Underwent neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by right modified radical mastectomy and postoperative radiotherapy
Noticed skin lesion after radiotherapy
Lesion did not respond to initial topical treatments
Presentation to dermatology 1 year after initial cancer diagnosis
Erythematous plaque measured 15 × 12 cm
Multiple palpable small nodules within the erythema
Immunohistochemistry negative for ER, PR, and HER2
Skin biopsy showed multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels

shortlist.label: Cutaneous metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: History of breast cancer and skin biopsy showing multiple emboli of carcinoma cells

shortlist.label: Inflammatory breast cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Presentation of erythematous plaque with multiple palpable small nodules, similar to inflammatory breast cancer

shortlist.label: Radiation dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of postoperative radiotherapy and development of skin lesion after radiation

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of breast cancer and radiation therapy, which are risk factors for angiosarcoma

shortlist.label: Stewart-Treves syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: History of breast cancer, mastectomy, and radiation therapy, which are risk factors for Stewart-Treves syndrome

raw.rationale: The presence of multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels on skin biopsy, along with a history of breast cancer, strongly supports the diagnosis of cutaneous metastasis.

rejected.label: Inflammatory breast cancer
rejected.why: Inflammatory breast cancer typically presents at the time of initial diagnosis, not a year later, and is less likely given the patient's previous treatments.

rejected.label: Radiation dermatitis
rejected.why: While radiation dermatitis could explain the erythema, it does not account for the presence of carcinoma cells in the skin biopsy.

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence provided in the vignette to support the diagnosis of angiosarcoma, such as characteristic vascular tumor cells on biopsy.

rejected.label: Stewart-Treves syndrome
rejected.why: Stewart-Treves syndrome refers to angiosarcoma arising in the context of chronic lymphedema, which is not indicated in the patient's history or presentation.
